name: THYROX 50 Tablet 120's
introduction:
Introduction About THYROX 50 TABLET

THYROX 50 TABLET contains Thyroxine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Synthetic thyroid hormones. It is used in the management of hypothyroidism. THYROX 50 TABLET is not recommended for use if you have unmanageed hyperthyroidism, unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis, unmanageed adrenal insufficiency, or pituitary insufficiency. Consult your doctor before taking it.

THYROX 50 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. Consult your doctor before taking it. THYROX 50 TABLET can be used safely in pregnant and breastfeeding women and requires dose adjustment. Consult your doctor before taking it.

The most common side effects of taking THYROX 50 TABLET are increased appetite, weight variations, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, changes in the menstrual cycle, fever, sensitivity to heat, cramps, and mood swings. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen.
usesDetails:
Uses Of THYROX 50 TABLET
To manage hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:
How THYROX 50 TABLET Works

THYROX 50 TABLET contains thyroxine, which controls the entire metabolic activity of the body and is very important for the proper functioning of our body.
usageDetails:
How to use THYROX 50 TABLET

Take THYROX 50 TABLET in the morning on an empty stomach at least half an hour before breakfast or as directed by the physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending on your age, body weight, and disease condition.
sideEffectsDetails:
Side Effects Of THYROX 50 TABLET
Common
Increased appetite
Weight variations
Headache
Vomiting, diarrhoea
Changes in the menstrual cycle
Fever
Sensitivity to heat
Cramps and mood swings

warnings.details: THYROX 50 TABLET can be used for women who are pregnant or are planning conception. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROX 50 TABLET can be used for breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROX 50 TABLET does not have any influence on the ability to drive or operate any machine.
THYROX 50 TABLET does not have any significant effect on patients with kidney disease. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROX 50 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with liver disease due to impaired metabolism. Consult your doctor before taking it.
Do not take THYROX 50 TABLET if you are allergic to thyroxine or any other ingredients in this medicine.

THYROX 50 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROX 50 TABLET is not recommended for use in children and neonates under 2 years of age. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROX 50 TABLET should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years and above). Consult your doctor before taking THYROX 50 TABLET.

Others

THYROX 50 TABLET is not recommended for use if you:

Have unmanageed hyperthyroidism
Have unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis
Have unmanageed adrenal insufficiency
Have unmanageed pituitary insufficiency

Before taking THYROX 50 TABLET, inform your doctor if you:

Have severe or chronic hypothyroidism
Have a history of thyroid cancer
Have diabetes mellitus or insipidus
Have pituitary and/or adrenocortical insufficiency
Have thyroid autonomy
Have secondary hypothyroidism or panhypopituitarism
Have a history of fits
Have myxoedema
Have malabsorption syndrome

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking THYROX 50 TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Cholestyramine, colestipol, clofibrate, simvastatin, and lovastatin (medicines used to manage high cholesterol levels in the blood)
Calcium, aluminium, magnesium, and iron supplements
Polystyrene sulfonates, kayexalate (used to manage high potassium levels in the blood)
Lanthanum, sevelamer (used to manage high phosphate levels in the blood)
Pantoprazole, rabeprazole, and sucralfate (medicines used to manage stomach ulcers)
Soya products and a high-fiber diet
Orlistat (a medicine used to reduce weight loss)
Propylthiouracil (used to manage hyperthyroidism)
Glucocorticoids (medicines used to manage inflammatory and autoimmune diseases) Ex. cortisone, prednisone
Propranolol (used to manage heart problems)
Lithium (used to manage mania)
Beta receptor blockers (medicines used to manage heart problems) Ex. propranolol, atenolol
Amiodarone (used to manage irregular heartbeats)
Iodinated contrast media (used in imaging techniques)
Salicylates (used to manage pain, fever, and inflammation) Ex. aspirin
Furosemide (used to manage heart problems)
Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin (used to manage fits)
Oestrogen based contraceptives (medicines used to manage fertilization) Ex. ethinylestradiol, norethindrone
Sertraline, amitriptyline, and imipramine (medicines used to manage depression)
Chloroquine or proguanil (used to manage malaria)
Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (Ex. imatinib and sunitinib)
Barbiturates
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum), an herbal medicine used to manage depression
Protease inhibitors, Ex. ritonavir (used to manage viral infections)
Methadone (used to manage pain)
5-flutouracil (used to manage cancer)
Coumarin derivatives (medicines used to manage blood clotting) Ex. warfarin
Digitalis (used to manage heart conditions)
Sympathomimetic agents (Ex. adrenaline), used to manage severe allergic reactions, cardiac arrest
Insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy Ex. metformin (used to manage diabetes mellitus)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more THYROX 50 TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Overdosage may cause hyperthyroidism, and symptoms include agitation, confusion, irritability, hyperactivity, headache, sweating, mydriasis, fast heartbeat, irregular heartbeat, fast breathing, fever, increased bowel movements, and fits. Psychiatric symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism may also occur, including affectability, fatigue, anxiety, and nervousness. In severe cases, it causes a thyrotoxic crisis and leads to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and coma.

name: Thyronorm 50mcg Tablet 120'S
introduction:
Introduction About THYRONORM 50MCG TABLET

Thyronorm 50mcg Tablet contains Levothyroxine Sodium, a synthetic thyroid hormone that supplements the body's natural hormone when the thyroid gland is underactive (hypothyroidism). It helps regulate metabolism, energy production, and overall physiological balance. 

THYRONORM 50MCG TABLET is not recommended for use if you have unmanageed hyperthyroidism, subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis, adrenal insufficiency, or pituitary insufficiency. Consult your doctor before taking it.

THYRONORM 50MCG TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. It  can be used safely in pregnant and breastfeeding women and requires dose adjustment.

Common side effects are increased appetite, weight variations, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, changes in the menstrual cycle, fever, sensitivity to heat, cramps, and mood swings. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen.
usesDetails:
Uses Of THYRONORM 50MCG TABLET
Manages hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:
How THYRONORM 50MCG TABLET Works
Levothyroxine is a synthetic form of thyroxine (T4), a natural thyroid hormone.
After oral administration, levothyroxine is absorbed primarily in the small intestine.
In peripheral tissues, T4 is converted into the active hormone triiodothyronine (T3) by deiodination.
T3 enters the cell nucleus and binds to thyroid hormone receptors.
This hormone-receptor complex modulates DNA transcription and protein synthesis essential for normal cellular metabolism.
These actions increase basal metabolic rate, stimulate gluconeogenesis, protein synthesis, and promote glycogen mobilization.
Levothyroxine thus restores deficient thyroid hormone levels and supports metabolic and physiological homeostasis.
The liver and kidneys play a key role in the metabolism and elimination of T4 and T3.
usageInstructions: Typical starting dose ranges from 25 to 50 mcg once daily, adjusted individually based on thyroid function tests and patient response.
The dose can vary between 25 to 200 mcg daily depending on severity and clinical monitoring.
Take Thyronorm on an empty stomach, ideally first thing in the morning.
Wait at least 30 to 60 minutes before eating breakfast or drinking tea/coffee.
Avoid food, milk, or other medications during this waiting period for optimal absorption.
Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water; do not crush or chew.
Maintain consistent timing daily to ensure stable hormone levels.
Separate Thyronorm dosing by at least 4 hours from antacids, calcium, iron, and some cholesterol-lowering medications to avoid interactions.
Regular blood testing is essential for dose adjustment and monitoring.
Thyronorm is usually taken once daily, preferably in the morning.
Therapy is often lifelong for hypothyroidism management.
Do not discontinue without consulting your healthcare provider, as symptoms may recur.
Food and certain beverages can reduce the absorption and efficacy of Thyronorm.
Taking the tablet on an empty stomach ensures maximum bioavailability.
Be aware of medications and supplements that can interfere with Thyronorm absorption and consult your doctor.

How to use THYRONORM 50MCG TABLET
Recommended Dosage of Thyronorm 50mcg
Typical starting dose ranges from 25 to 50 mcg once daily, adjusted individually based on thyroid function tests and patient response.
The dose can vary between 25 to 200 mcg daily depending on severity and clinical monitoring.
When to Take Thyronorm: Timing with Meals
Take Thyronorm on an empty stomach, ideally first thing in the morning.
Wait at least 30 to 60 minutes before eating breakfast or drinking tea/coffee.
Avoid food, milk, or other medications during this waiting period for optimal absorption.
Important Administration Tips for Thyronorm Tablet
Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water; do not crush or chew.
Maintain consistent timing daily to ensure stable hormone levels.
Separate Thyronorm dosing by at least 4 hours from antacids, calcium, iron, and some cholesterol-lowering medications to avoid interactions.
Regular blood testing is essential for dose adjustment and monitoring.
Duration and Frequency of Thyronorm Use
Thyronorm is usually taken once daily, preferably in the morning.
Therapy is often lifelong for hypothyroidism management.
Do not discontinue without consulting your healthcare provider, as symptoms may recur.
Thyronorm Tablet and Food: What You Should Know
Food and certain beverages can reduce the absorption and efficacy of Thyronorm.
Taking the tablet on an empty stomach ensures maximum bioavailability.
Be aware of medications and supplements that can interfere with Thyronorm absorption and consult your doctor.

moreInfo:
More Information
Did you know?
Levothyroxine, the active ingredient in Thyronorm, is one of the most widely prescribed medications worldwide for managing hypothyroidism, helping millions maintain normal metabolism and energy balance.
Despite being a synthetic hormone, levothyroxine closely mimics the natural thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4) and relies on the body's conversion to triiodothyronine (T3) to exert its effects at the cellular level.
Proper timing of Thyronorm dosing taking it on an empty stomach and waiting before meals can significantly impact its absorption and effectiveness.
Patients on levothyroxine therapy regularly monitor thyroid hormone levels through blood tests to ensure optimal dosing and avoid side effects.
Drug interactions with supplements like calcium and iron, or medications such as antacids and anticonvulsants, can affect levothyroxine absorption, requiring careful management and dose adjustments.
Levothyroxine therapy may continue lifelong for many individuals, but with appropriate medical follow-up, it substantially improves quality of life and metabolic health.

name: Thyronorm 25Mcg Tablet 120'S
introduction:
Introduction About THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET

THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET contains Thyroxine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Synthetic thyroid hormones. It is used in the management of hypothyroidism. THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET is not recommended for use if you have unmanageed hyperthyroidism, unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis, unmanageed adrenal insufficiency, or pituitary insufficiency. Consult your doctor before taking it.

THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. Consult your doctor before taking it. THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET can be used safely in pregnant and breastfeeding women and requires dose adjustment. Consult your doctor before taking it.

The most common side effects of taking THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET are increased appetite, weight variations, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, changes in the menstrual cycle, fever, sensitivity to heat, cramps, and mood swings. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen.
usesDetails:
Uses Of THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET
To manage hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:
How THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET Works

THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET contains thyroxine, which controls the entire metabolic activity of the body and is very important for the proper functioning of our body.
usageDetails:
How to use THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET

Take THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET in the morning on an empty stomach at least half an hour before breakfast or as directed by the physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending on your age, body weight, and disease condition.
sideEffectsDetails:
Side Effects Of THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET
Common
Increased appetite
Weight variations
Headache
Vomiting, diarrhoea
Changes in the menstrual cycle
Fever
Sensitivity to heat
Cramps and mood swings

Others

Have diabetes mellitus or insipidus

Have thyroid autonomy
Have secondary hypothyroidism or panhypopituitarism
Have a history of fits
Have myxoedema
Have malabsorption syndrome

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Cholestyramine, colestipol, clofibrate, simvastatin, and lovastatin (medicines used to manage high cholesterol levels in the blood)
Calcium, aluminium, magnesium, and iron supplements
Polystyrene sulfonates, kayexalate (used to manage high potassium levels in the blood)
Lanthanum, sevelamer (used to manage high phosphate levels in the blood)
Pantoprazole, rabeprazole, and sucralfate (medicines used to manage stomach ulcers)
Soya products and a high-fiber diet
Orlistat (a medicine used to reduce weight loss)
Propylthiouracil (used to manage hyperthyroidism)
Glucocorticoids (medicines used to manage inflammatory and autoimmune diseases) Ex. cortisone, prednisone
Propranolol (used to manage heart problems)
Lithium (used to manage mania)
Beta receptor blockers (medicines used to manage heart problems) Ex. propranolol, atenolol
Amiodarone (used to manage irregular heartbeats)
Iodinated contrast media (used in imaging techniques)
Salicylates (used to manage pain, fever, and inflammation) Ex. aspirin
Furosemide (used to manage heart problems)
Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin (used to manage fits)
Oestrogen based contraceptives (medicines used to manage fertilization) Ex. ethinylestradiol, norethindrone
Sertraline, amitriptyline, and imipramine (medicines used to manage depression)
Chloroquine or proguanil (used to manage malaria)
Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (Ex. imatinib and sunitinib)
Barbiturates
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum), an herbal medicine used to manage depression
Protease inhibitors, Ex. ritonavir (used to manage viral infections)
Methadone (used to manage pain)
5-flutouracil (used to manage cancer)
Coumarin derivatives (medicines used to manage blood clotting) Ex. warfarin
Digitalis (used to manage heart conditions)
Sympathomimetic agents (Ex. adrenaline), used to manage severe allergic reactions, cardiac arrest
Insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy Ex. metformin (used to manage diabetes mellitus)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Overdosage may cause hyperthyroidism, and symptoms include agitation, confusion, irritability, hyperactivity, headache, sweating, mydriasis, fast heartbeat, irregular heartbeat, fast breathing, fever, increased bowel movements, and fits. Psychiatric symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism may also occur, including affectability, fatigue, anxiety, and nervousness. In severe cases, it causes a thyrotoxic crisis and leads to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and coma.

More Information
Storage
Keep THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET out of the sight and reach of children
Store THYRONORM 25MCG TABLET below 25°C

name: Euthyrox 25Mcg Tablet 100'S
introduction:
Introduction About EUTHYROX 25MCG TABLET

EUTHYROX 25MCG TABLET contains Levothyroxine which belong to the group of medicines known as Thyroid hormones. It is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is chemically identical to thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland. It helps in replacing missing thyroid hormone and in all forms of underactive thyroid function (hypothyroidism) or after the removal of the thyroid gland.  Thyroid hormone is vital for the normal growth and development. Lack of right number of thyroid hormones leads to slowing down in natural functions of our body.

Hypothyroidism is a condition where enough thyroid hormone required are not produced by the body. Some of the most common symptoms of hypothyroidism are tiredness, weight gain and feeling depressed. EUTHYROX 25MCG TABLET helps in replacing the thyroxine that your thyroid gland cannot produce and manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism. Always take EUTHYROX 25MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 

Before taking this medicine tell your doctor if you have or ever had kidney disease, heart disease, or pancreas problems. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. The most common side effects such as restlessness, insomnia, diarrhea, changes in menstrual cycle in women. Consult your doctor for advice if you experience any above side effects or it persists for a longer duration.
uses: In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce
To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism
usesDetails:

mechanismOfAction:
How EUTHYROX 25MCG TABLET Works

EUTHYROX 25MCG TABLET is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is identical to natural occurring thyroid hormone thyroxine or T4, produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine regulates the production of another hormone called thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) which in turn controls how much thyroxine is produced. Levothyroxine regulates TSH production in the same way and therefore, substitutes for a lack of endogenous thyroxine (produced by the thyroid gland).

Take EUTHYROX 25MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush the medicine. Your doctor will prescribe the right dose depends on your age, body weight and disease condition.

introduction:
Introduction About EUTHYROX 75MCG TABLET

EUTHYROX 75MCG TABLET contains Levothyroxine which belong to the group of medicines known as Thyroid hormones. It is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is chemically identical to thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland. It helps in replacing missing thyroid hormone and in all forms of underactive thyroid function (hypothyroidism) or after the removal of the thyroid gland.  Thyroid hormone is vital for the normal growth and development. Lack of right number of thyroid hormones leads to slowing down in natural functions of our body.

Hypothyroidism is a condition where enough thyroid hormone required are not produced by the body. Some of the most common symptoms of hypothyroidism are tiredness, weight gain and feeling depressed. EUTHYROX 75MCG TABLET helps in replacing the thyroxine that your thyroid gland cannot produce and manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism. Always take EUTHYROX 75MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 

Before taking this medicine tell your doctor if you have or ever had kidney disease, heart disease, or pancreas problems. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. The most common side effects such as restlessness, insomnia, diarrhea, changes in menstrual cycle in women. Consult your doctor for advice if you experience any above side effects or it persists for a longer duration.

mechanismOfAction:
How EUTHYROX 75MCG TABLET Works

EUTHYROX 75MCG TABLET is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is identical to natural occurring thyroid hormone thyroxine or T4, produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine regulates the production of another hormone called thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) which in turn controls how much thyroxine is produced. Levothyroxine regulates TSH production in the same way and therefore, substitutes for a lack of endogenous thyroxine (produced by the thyroid gland).

Take EUTHYROX 75MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush the medicine. Your doctor will prescribe the right dose depends on your age, body weight and disease condition.

name: Euthyrox 50mcg Tablet 100'S
introduction:
Introduction About EUTHYROX 50MCG TABLET

EUTHYROX 50MCG TABLET contains Levothyroxine which belong to the group of medicines known as Thyroid hormones. It is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is chemically identical to thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland. It helps in replacing missing thyroid hormone and in all forms of underactive thyroid function (hypothyroidism) or after the removal of the thyroid gland.  Thyroid hormone is vital for the normal growth and development. Lack of right number of thyroid hormones leads to slowing down in natural functions of our body.

Hypothyroidism is a condition where enough thyroid hormone required are not produced by the body. Some of the most common symptoms of hypothyroidism are tiredness, weight gain and feeling depressed. EUTHYROX 50MCG TABLET helps in replacing the thyroxine that your thyroid gland cannot produce and manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism. Always take EUTHYROX 50MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 

Before taking this medicine tell your doctor if you have or ever had kidney disease, heart disease, or pancreas problems. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. The most common side effects such as restlessness, insomnia, diarrhea, changes in menstrual cycle in women. Consult your doctor for advice if you experience any above side effects or it persists for a longer duration.
uses: In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce
To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism
usesDetails:

It helps:

In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce
To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:
How EUTHYROX 50MCG TABLET Works

EUTHYROX 50MCG TABLET is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is identical to natural occurring thyroid hormone thyroxine or T4, produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine regulates the production of another hormone called thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) which in turn controls how much thyroxine is produced. Levothyroxine regulates TSH production in the same way and therefore, substitutes for a lack of endogenous thyroxine (produced by the thyroid gland).
usageDetails:
How to use EUTHYROX 50MCG TABLET

Take EUTHYROX 50MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush the medicine. Your doctor will prescribe the right dose depends on your age, body weight and disease condition.

name: Lethyrox 12.5Mcg Tablet 50'S
introduction:
Introduction About LETHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET

LETHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET contains Levothyroxine which belong to the group of medicines known as Thyroid hormones. It is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is chemically identical to thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland. It helps in replacing missing thyroid hormone and in all forms of underactive thyroid function (hypothyroidism) or after the removal of the thyroid gland.  Thyroid hormone is vital for the normal growth and development. Lack of right number of thyroid hormones leads to slowing down in natural functions of our body.

Hypothyroidism is a condition where enough thyroid hormone required are not produced by the body. Some of the most common symptoms of hypothyroidism are tiredness, weight gain and feeling depressed. LETHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET helps in replacing the thyroxine that your thyroid gland cannot produce and manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism. Always take LETHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 

Before taking this medicine tell your doctor if you have or ever had kidney disease, heart disease, or pancreas problems. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. The most common side effects such as restlessness, insomnia, diarrhea, changes in menstrual cycle in women. Consult your doctor for advice if you experience any above side effects or it persists for a longer duration.
uses: In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce
To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism

mechanismOfAction:
How LETHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET Works

LETHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is identical to natural occurring thyroid hormone thyroxine or T4, produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine regulates the production of another hormone called thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) which in turn controls how much thyroxine is produced. Levothyroxine regulates TSH production in the same way and therefore, substitutes for a lack of endogenous thyroxine (produced by the thyroid gland).

THYROX 37.5 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. usesDetails:

To manage hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:
How THYROX 37.5 TABLET Works

THYROX 37.5 TABLET contains thyroxine, which controls the entire metabolic activity of the body and is very important for the proper functioning of our body.
usageDetails:
How to use THYROX 37.5 TABLET

Take THYROX 37.5 TABLET in the morning on an empty stomach at least half an hour before breakfast or as directed by the physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending on your age, body weight, and disease condition.

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking THYROX 37.5 TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Cholestyramine, colestipol, clofibrate, simvastatin, and lovastatin (medicines used to manage high cholesterol levels in the blood)
Calcium, aluminium, magnesium, and iron supplements
Polystyrene sulfonates, kayexalate (used to manage high potassium levels in the blood)
Lanthanum, sevelamer (used to manage high phosphate levels in the blood)
Pantoprazole, rabeprazole, and sucralfate (medicines used to manage stomach ulcers)
Soya products and a high-fiber diet
Orlistat (a medicine used to reduce weight loss)
Propylthiouracil (used to manage hyperthyroidism)
Glucocorticoids (medicines used to manage inflammatory and autoimmune diseases) Ex. cortisone, prednisone
Propranolol (used to manage heart problems)
Lithium (used to manage mania)
Beta receptor blockers (medicines used to manage heart problems) Ex. propranolol, atenolol
Amiodarone (used to manage irregular heartbeats)
Iodinated contrast media (used in imaging techniques)
Salicylates (used to manage pain, fever, and inflammation) Ex. aspirin
Furosemide (used to manage heart problems)
Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin (used to manage fits)
Oestrogen based contraceptives (medicines used to manage fertilization) Ex. ethinylestradiol, norethindrone
Sertraline, amitriptyline, and imipramine (medicines used to manage depression)
Chloroquine or proguanil (used to manage malaria)
Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (Ex. imatinib and sunitinib)
Barbiturates
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum), an herbal medicine used to manage depression
Protease inhibitors, Ex. ritonavir (used to manage viral infections)
Methadone (used to manage pain)
5-flutouracil (used to manage cancer)
Coumarin derivatives (medicines used to manage blood clotting) Ex. warfarin
Digitalis (used to manage heart conditions)
Sympathomimetic agents (Ex. adrenaline), used to manage severe allergic reactions, cardiac arrest
Insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy Ex. metformin (used to manage diabetes mellitus)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more THYROX 37.5 TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Overdosage may cause hyperthyroidism, and symptoms include agitation, confusion, irritability, hyperactivity, headache, sweating, mydriasis, fast heartbeat, irregular heartbeat, fast breathing, fever, increased bowel movements, and fits. Psychiatric symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism may also occur, including affectability, fatigue, anxiety, and nervousness. In severe cases, it causes a thyrotoxic crisis and leads to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and coma.

name: Euthyrox 100mcg Tablet 100'S
introduction:
Introduction About EUTHYROX 100MCG TABLET

EUTHYROX 100MCG TABLET contains Levothyroxine which belong to the group of medicines known as Thyroid hormones. It is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is chemically identical to thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland. It helps in replacing missing thyroid hormone and in all forms of underactive thyroid function (hypothyroidism) or after the removal of the thyroid gland.  Thyroid hormone is vital for the normal growth and development. Lack of right number of thyroid hormones leads to slowing down in natural functions of our body.

Hypothyroidism is a condition where enough thyroid hormone required are not produced by the body. Some of the most common symptoms of hypothyroidism are tiredness, weight gain and feeling depressed. EUTHYROX 100MCG TABLET helps in replacing the thyroxine that your thyroid gland cannot produce and manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism. Always take EUTHYROX 100MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 

Before taking this medicine tell your doctor if you have or ever had kidney disease, heart disease, or pancreas problems. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. The most common side effects such as restlessness, insomnia, diarrhea, changes in menstrual cycle in women. Consult your doctor for advice if you experience any above side effects or it persists for a longer duration.
uses: In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce
To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism
usesDetails:
Uses Of EUTHYROX 100MCG TABLET

It helps:

In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce
To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:
How EUTHYROX 100MCG TABLET Works

EUTHYROX 100MCG TABLET is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is identical to natural occurring thyroid hormone thyroxine or T4, produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine regulates the production of another hormone called thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) which in turn controls how much thyroxine is produced. Levothyroxine regulates TSH production in the same way and therefore, substitutes for a lack of endogenous thyroxine (produced by the thyroid gland).

How to use EUTHYROX 100MCG TABLET

Take EUTHYROX 100MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush the medicine. Your doctor will prescribe the right dose depends on your age, body weight and disease condition.

Interactions

A. Drug-Drug Interaction:

Tell your doctor if you are taking or recently taken any other medicines, including medicines obtained without a prescription or the following:

Medicines used to manage diabetes
Anticoagulants such as warfarin, dicoumarol (used to thin the blood)
Amiodarone (used to manage some heart conditions)
Aspirin
Medicines containing oestrogen (e.g. used for hormone replacement therapy or oral contraceptives)
Antidepressants (e.g. sertraline and tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline, imipramine)
Chloroquine and proguanil (used in malaria and rheumatic diseases)

Medicines used to control the heart rate (such as digoxin)

name: LINORMA T3 5mcg Tablet 100's
introduction:
Introduction About LINORMA T3 5MCG TABLET

LINORMA T3 5MCG TABLET contains Liothyronine which belongs to the group of medicines called Anti- thyroid agents. It is used for mild to severe hypothyroidism (thyroid gland does not produce enough hormone) and enlarged thyroid gland (simple goiter). LINORMA T3 5MCG TABLET is a synthetic form of a hormone produced by the thyroid gland called triiodothyronine.

LINORMA T3 5MCG TABLET is not recommended for patients with heart problems. It should be used with caution in patients with uncorrected adrenal gland under-activity, problem with thyroid (myxedema), or adrenal or pituitary gland, high blood sugar, bone thinning and blood clotting problem. Consult your doctor if you are a pregnant or a breastfeeding women.

The common side effects of taking this medicine are headache, excessive sweating, fatigue, increased appetite, weight loss, fever and diarrhea. Consult your doctor if any of the above side persists for a longer duration.
uses: Mild to severe hypothyroidism (thyroid gland does not produce enough hormone)
usesDetails:
Uses Of LINORMA T3 5MCG TABLET

It is used for:

Mild to severe hypothyroidism (thyroid gland does not produce enough hormone)
Enlarged thyroid gland (simple goiter)
mechanismOfAction:
How LINORMA T3 5MCG TABLET Works

Thyroid hormones exert their physiologic actions through control of DNA transcription and protein synthesis. Triiodothyronine (T3) and L-thyroxine (T4) diffuse into the cell nucleus and bind to thyroid receptor proteins attached to DNA. This hormone nuclear receptor complex activates gene transcription and synthesis of messenger RNA and cytoplasmic proteins. The physiological actions of thyroid hormones are produced predominantly by T3, the majority of which (approximately 80%) is derived from T4 by deiodination in peripheral tissues.
usageDetails:
How to use LINORMA T3 5MCG TABLET

Take LINORMA T3 5MCG TABLET as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.
sideEffects: Cardiac arrhythmias (heartbeat which are irregular or too fast)

The clinical experience does not indicate any adverse effect on fetuses when thyroid hormones are administered to pregnant women. Blood clotting problem

name: THYROUP 100mcg Tablet 120's
introduction:
Introduction About THYROUP 100MCG TABLET

THYROUP 100MCG TABLET contains Thyroxine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Synthetic thyroid hormones. It is used in the management of hypothyroidism. THYROUP 100MCG TABLET is not recommended for use if you have unmanageed hyperthyroidism, unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis, unmanageed adrenal insufficiency, or pituitary insufficiency. Consult your doctor before taking it.

THYROUP 100MCG TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. Consult your doctor before taking it. THYROUP 100MCG TABLET can be used safely in pregnant and breastfeeding women and requires dose adjustment. Consult your doctor before taking it.

The most common side effects of taking THYROUP 100MCG TABLET are increased appetite, weight variations, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, changes in the menstrual cycle, fever, sensitivity to heat, cramps, and mood swings. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen.
usesDetails:
Uses Of THYROUP 100MCG TABLET
To manage hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:
How THYROUP 100MCG TABLET Works

THYROUP 100MCG TABLET contains thyroxine, which controls the entire metabolic activity of the body and is very important for the proper functioning of our body.
usageDetails:
How to use THYROUP 100MCG TABLET

Take THYROUP 100MCG TABLET in the morning on an empty stomach at least half an hour before breakfast or as directed by the physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending on your age, body weight, and disease condition.
sideEffectsDetails:
Side Effects Of THYROUP 100MCG TABLET
Common
Increased appetite
Weight variations
Headache
Vomiting, diarrhoea
Changes in the menstrual cycle
Fever
Sensitivity to heat
Cramps and mood swings

warnings.details: THYROUP 100MCG TABLET can be used for women who are pregnant or are planning conception. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROUP 100MCG TABLET can be used for breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROUP 100MCG TABLET does not have any influence on the ability to drive or operate any machine.
THYROUP 100MCG TABLET does not have any significant effect on patients with kidney disease. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROUP 100MCG TABLET should be used with caution in patients with liver disease due to impaired metabolism. Consult your doctor before taking it.
Do not take THYROUP 100MCG TABLET if you are allergic to thyroxine or any other ingredients in this medicine.

THYROUP 100MCG TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROUP 100MCG TABLET is not recommended for use in children and neonates under 2 years of age. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYROUP 100MCG TABLET should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years and above). Consult your doctor before taking THYROUP 100MCG TABLET.

Others

THYROUP 100MCG TABLET is not recommended for use if you:

Have unmanageed hyperthyroidism
Have unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis
Have unmanageed adrenal insufficiency
Have unmanageed pituitary insufficiency

Before taking THYROUP 100MCG TABLET, inform your doctor if you:

Have severe or chronic hypothyroidism
Have a history of thyroid cancer
Have diabetes mellitus or insipidus
Have pituitary and/or adrenocortical insufficiency
Have thyroid autonomy
Have secondary hypothyroidism or panhypopituitarism
Have a history of fits
Have myxoedema
Have malabsorption syndrome

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking THYROUP 100MCG TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Cholestyramine, colestipol, clofibrate, simvastatin, and lovastatin (medicines used to manage high cholesterol levels in the blood)
Calcium, aluminium, magnesium, and iron supplements
Polystyrene sulfonates, kayexalate (used to manage high potassium levels in the blood)
Lanthanum, sevelamer (used to manage high phosphate levels in the blood)
Pantoprazole, rabeprazole, and sucralfate (medicines used to manage stomach ulcers)
Soya products and a high-fiber diet
Orlistat (a medicine used to reduce weight loss)
Propylthiouracil (used to manage hyperthyroidism)
Glucocorticoids (medicines used to manage inflammatory and autoimmune diseases) Ex. cortisone, prednisone
Propranolol (used to manage heart problems)
Lithium (used to manage mania)
Beta receptor blockers (medicines used to manage heart problems) Ex. propranolol, atenolol
Amiodarone (used to manage irregular heartbeats)
Iodinated contrast media (used in imaging techniques)
Salicylates (used to manage pain, fever, and inflammation) Ex. aspirin
Furosemide (used to manage heart problems)
Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin (used to manage fits)
Oestrogen based contraceptives (medicines used to manage fertilization) Ex. ethinylestradiol, norethindrone
Sertraline, amitriptyline, and imipramine (medicines used to manage depression)
Chloroquine or proguanil (used to manage malaria)
Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (Ex. imatinib and sunitinib)
Barbiturates
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum), an herbal medicine used to manage depression
Protease inhibitors, Ex. ritonavir (used to manage viral infections)
Methadone (used to manage pain)
5-flutouracil (used to manage cancer)
Coumarin derivatives (medicines used to manage blood clotting) Ex. warfarin
Digitalis (used to manage heart conditions)
Sympathomimetic agents (Ex. adrenaline), used to manage severe allergic reactions, cardiac arrest
Insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy Ex. metformin (used to manage diabetes mellitus)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more THYROUP 100MCG TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Overdosage may cause hyperthyroidism, and symptoms include agitation, confusion, irritability, hyperactivity, headache, sweating, mydriasis, fast heartbeat, irregular heartbeat, fast breathing, fever, increased bowel movements, and fits. Psychiatric symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism may also occur, including affectability, fatigue, anxiety, and nervousness. In severe cases, it causes a thyrotoxic crisis and leads to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and coma.

Keep THYROUP 100MCG TABLET out of the sight and reach of children
Store THYROUP 100MCG TABLET below 25°C

name: THYROUP 150mcg Tablet 120's
introduction:
Introduction About THYROUP 150MCG TABLET

THYROUP 150MCG TABLET contains Levothyroxine which belong to the group of medicines known as Thyroid hormones. It is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is chemically identical to thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland. It helps in replacing missing thyroid hormone and in all forms of underactive thyroid function (hypothyroidism) or after the removal of the thyroid gland.  Thyroid hormone is vital for the normal growth and development. Lack of right number of thyroid hormones leads to slowing down in natural functions of our body.

Hypothyroidism is a condition where enough thyroid hormone required are not produced by the body. Some of the most common symptoms of hypothyroidism are tiredness, weight gain and feeling depressed. THYROUP 150MCG TABLET helps in replacing the thyroxine that your thyroid gland cannot produce and manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism. Always take THYROUP 150MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 

Before taking this medicine tell your doctor if you have or ever had kidney disease, heart disease, or pancreas problems. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. The most common side effects such as restlessness, insomnia, diarrhea, changes in menstrual cycle in women. Consult your doctor for advice if you experience any above side effects or it persists for a longer duration.
uses: In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce
To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism
usesDetails:

In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce

mechanismOfAction:
How THYROUP 150MCG TABLET Works

THYROUP 150MCG TABLET is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is identical to natural occurring thyroid hormone thyroxine or T4, produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine regulates the production of another hormone called thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) which in turn controls how much thyroxine is produced. Levothyroxine regulates TSH production in the same way and therefore, substitutes for a lack of endogenous thyroxine (produced by the thyroid gland).

Take THYROUP 150MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush the medicine. Your doctor will prescribe the right dose depends on your age, body weight and disease condition.

usageDetails:

Take THYRONEED 25 TABLET in the morning on an empty stomach at least half an hour before breakfast or as directed by the physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending on your age, body weight, and disease condition.

THYRONEED 25 TABLET does not have any influence on the ability to drive or operate any machine.
THYRONEED 25 TABLET does not have any significant effect on patients with kidney disease. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYRONEED 25 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with liver disease due to impaired metabolism. Consult your doctor before taking it.
Do not take THYRONEED 25 TABLET if you are allergic to thyroxine or any other ingredients in this medicine.

THYRONEED 25 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYRONEED 25 TABLET is not recommended for use in children and neonates under 2 years of age. Consult your doctor before taking it.
THYRONEED 25 TABLET should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years and above). Consult your doctor before taking THYRONEED 25 TABLET.

Others

THYRONEED 25 TABLET is not recommended for use if you:

Have unmanageed hyperthyroidism
Have unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis
Have unmanageed adrenal insufficiency
Have unmanageed pituitary insufficiency

Before taking THYRONEED 25 TABLET, inform your doctor if you:

Have severe or chronic hypothyroidism
Have a history of thyroid cancer
Have diabetes mellitus or insipidus
Have pituitary and/or adrenocortical insufficiency
Have thyroid autonomy
Have secondary hypothyroidism or panhypopituitarism
Have a history of fits
Have myxoedema
Have malabsorption syndrome

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking THYRONEED 25 TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Cholestyramine, colestipol, clofibrate, simvastatin, and lovastatin (medicines used to manage high cholesterol levels in the blood)
Calcium, aluminium, magnesium, and iron supplements
Polystyrene sulfonates, kayexalate (used to manage high potassium levels in the blood)
Lanthanum, sevelamer (used to manage high phosphate levels in the blood)
Pantoprazole, rabeprazole, and sucralfate (medicines used to manage stomach ulcers)
Soya products and a high-fiber diet
Orlistat (a medicine used to reduce weight loss)
Propylthiouracil (used to manage hyperthyroidism)
Glucocorticoids (medicines used to manage inflammatory and autoimmune diseases) Ex. cortisone, prednisone
Propranolol (used to manage heart problems)
Lithium (used to manage mania)
Beta receptor blockers (medicines used to manage heart problems) Ex. propranolol, atenolol
Amiodarone (used to manage irregular heartbeats)
Iodinated contrast media (used in imaging techniques)
Salicylates (used to manage pain, fever, and inflammation) Ex. aspirin
Furosemide (used to manage heart problems)
Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin (used to manage fits)
Oestrogen based contraceptives (medicines used to manage fertilization) Ex. ethinylestradiol, norethindrone
Sertraline, amitriptyline, and imipramine (medicines used to manage depression)
Chloroquine or proguanil (used to manage malaria)
Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (Ex. imatinib and sunitinib)
Barbiturates
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum), an herbal medicine used to manage depression
Protease inhibitors, Ex. ritonavir (used to manage viral infections)
Methadone (used to manage pain)
5-flutouracil (used to manage cancer)
Coumarin derivatives (medicines used to manage blood clotting) Ex. warfarin
Digitalis (used to manage heart conditions)
Sympathomimetic agents (Ex. adrenaline), used to manage severe allergic reactions, cardiac arrest
Insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy Ex. metformin (used to manage diabetes mellitus)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more THYRONEED 25 TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Overdosage may cause hyperthyroidism, and symptoms include agitation, confusion, irritability, hyperactivity, headache, sweating, mydriasis, fast heartbeat, irregular heartbeat, fast breathing, fever, increased bowel movements, and fits. Psychiatric symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism may also occur, including affectability, fatigue, anxiety, and nervousness. In severe cases, it causes a thyrotoxic crisis and leads to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and coma.

introduction:
Introduction About LINORMA T3 TABLET

LINORMA T3 TABLET contains Liothyronine which belongs to the group of medicines called Anti- thyroid agents. It is used for mild to severe hypothyroidism (thyroid gland does not produce enough hormone) and enlarged thyroid gland (simple goiter). LINORMA T3 TABLET is a synthetic form of a hormone produced by the thyroid gland called triiodothyronine.

LINORMA T3 TABLET is not recommended for patients with heart problems. It should be used with caution in patients with uncorrected adrenal gland under-activity, problem with thyroid (myxedema), or adrenal or pituitary gland, high blood sugar, bone thinning and blood clotting problem. Consult your doctor if you are a pregnant or a breastfeeding women.

The common side effects of taking this medicine are headache, excessive sweating, fatigue, increased appetite, weight loss, fever and diarrhea. Consult your doctor if any of the above side persists for a longer duration.
uses: Mild to severe hypothyroidism (thyroid gland does not produce enough hormone)
usesDetails:

It is used for:

Mild to severe hypothyroidism (thyroid gland does not produce enough hormone)
Enlarged thyroid gland (simple goiter)
mechanismOfAction:
How LINORMA T3 TABLET Works

Thyroid hormones exert their physiologic actions through control of DNA transcription and protein synthesis. Triiodothyronine (T3) and L-thyroxine (T4) diffuse into the cell nucleus and bind to thyroid receptor proteins attached to DNA. This hormone nuclear receptor complex activates gene transcription and synthesis of messenger RNA and cytoplasmic proteins. The physiological actions of thyroid hormones are produced predominantly by T3, the majority of which (approximately 80%) is derived from T4 by deiodination in peripheral tissues.
usageDetails:
How to use LINORMA T3 TABLET

Take LINORMA T3 TABLET as advised by your physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not crush or chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

warnings.details: Thyroid hormones do not readily cross the placental barrier. The clinical experience does not indicate any adverse effect on fetuses when thyroid hormones are administered to pregnant women. Thyroid replacement therapy to hypothyroid women should not be discontinued during pregnancy. Consult your doctor before taking the medicine.
LINORMA T3 TABLET should be used with caution in breastfeeding women. Consult your doctor before taking the medicine.
LINORMA T3 TABLET should be used with caution in patients with kidney disease. Consult your doctor before taking the medicine.
LINORMA T3 TABLET is not recommended for use in patients with acute liver diseases or increased serum transaminase levels. Consult your doctor before taking the medicine.
Do not take LINORMA T3 TABLET if you are allergic or hypersensitive to or any other ingredients of this medicine.

LINORMA T3 TABLET is not recommended for patients with acute myocardial infarction (heart attack). It should be used with caution in patients with angina pectoris (chest pain). Consult your doctor for advice.
Clinical assessment of growth, development, and thyroid status should be monitored frequently in children. Consult your doctor for advice before giving to your child.
LINORMA T3 TABLET should be caution in patients with impaired renal function. Care should be taken in dose selection and renal function should be monitored.

Others

LINORMA T3 TABLET is not recommended if you have:

Uncorrected adrenal gland under-activity
A history problem with thyroid (myxedema), or adrenal or pituitary gland
High blood sugar (diabetes)
Decreased development of sexual organs (hypogonadism)
Bone thinning (osteoporosis)
Blood clotting problem

name: Euthyrox 88Mcg Tablet 100'S
introduction:
Introduction About EUTHYROX 88MCG TABLET

EUTHYROX 88MCG TABLET contains Levothyroxine which belong to the group of medicines known as Thyroid hormones. It is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is chemically identical to thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland. It helps in replacing missing thyroid hormone and in all forms of underactive thyroid function (hypothyroidism) or after the removal of the thyroid gland.  Thyroid hormone is vital for the normal growth and development. Lack of right number of thyroid hormones leads to slowing down in natural functions of our body.

Hypothyroidism is a condition where enough thyroid hormone required are not produced by the body. Some of the most common symptoms of hypothyroidism are tiredness, weight gain and feeling depressed. EUTHYROX 88MCG TABLET helps in replacing the thyroxine that your thyroid gland cannot produce and manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism. Always take EUTHYROX 88MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 

Before taking this medicine tell your doctor if you have or ever had kidney disease, heart disease, or pancreas problems. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. The most common side effects such as restlessness, insomnia, diarrhea, changes in menstrual cycle in women. Consult your doctor for advice if you experience any above side effects or it persists for a longer duration.

To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism

mechanismOfAction:
How EUTHYROX 88MCG TABLET Works

EUTHYROX 88MCG TABLET is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is identical to natural occurring thyroid hormone thyroxine or T4, produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine regulates the production of another hormone called thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) which in turn controls how much thyroxine is produced. Levothyroxine regulates TSH production in the same way and therefore, substitutes for a lack of endogenous thyroxine (produced by the thyroid gland).

Take EUTHYROX 88MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush the medicine. Your doctor will prescribe the right dose depends on your age, body weight and disease condition.

Tell your doctor if you are taking or recently taken any other medicines, including medicines obtained without a prescription or the following:

Medicines used to manage diabetes
Anticoagulants such as warfarin, dicoumarol (used to thin the blood)
Amiodarone (used to manage some heart conditions)
Aspirin

name: EUTHYROX 12.5mcg Tablet 100's
introduction:
Introduction About EUTHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET

EUTHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET contains Levothyroxine which belong to the group of medicines known as Thyroid hormones. It is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is chemically identical to thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland. It helps in replacing missing thyroid hormone and in all forms of underactive thyroid function (hypothyroidism) or after the removal of the thyroid gland.  Thyroid hormone is vital for the normal growth and development. Lack of right number of thyroid hormones leads to slowing down in natural functions of our body.

Hypothyroidism is a condition where enough thyroid hormone required are not produced by the body. Some of the most common symptoms of hypothyroidism are tiredness, weight gain and feeling depressed. EUTHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET helps in replacing the thyroxine that your thyroid gland cannot produce and manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism. Always take EUTHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 

Before taking this medicine tell your doctor if you have or ever had kidney disease, heart disease, or pancreas problems. mechanismOfAction:
How EUTHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET Works

EUTHYROX 12.5MCG TABLET is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is identical to natural occurring thyroid hormone thyroxine or T4, produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine regulates the production of another hormone called thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) which in turn controls how much thyroxine is produced. Levothyroxine regulates TSH production in the same way and therefore, substitutes for a lack of endogenous thyroxine (produced by the thyroid gland).

introduction:
Introduction About THYROACTIV 75MG TABLET

THYROACTIV 75MG TABLET contains Thyroxine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Synthetic thyroid hormones. It is used in the management of hypothyroidism. THYROACTIV 75MG TABLET is not recommended for use if you have unmanageed hyperthyroidism, unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis, unmanageed adrenal insufficiency, or pituitary insufficiency. Consult your doctor before taking it.

THYROACTIV 75MG TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. Consult your doctor before taking it. THYROACTIV 75MG TABLET can be used safely in pregnant and breastfeeding women and requires dose adjustment. Consult your doctor before taking it.

The most common side effects of taking THYROACTIV 75MG TABLET are increased appetite, weight variations, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, changes in the menstrual cycle, fever, sensitivity to heat, cramps, and mood swings. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen.

To manage hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking THYROACTIV 75MG TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Cholestyramine, colestipol, clofibrate, simvastatin, and lovastatin (medicines used to manage high cholesterol levels in the blood)
Calcium, aluminium, magnesium, and iron supplements
Polystyrene sulfonates, kayexalate (used to manage high potassium levels in the blood)
Lanthanum, sevelamer (used to manage high phosphate levels in the blood)
Pantoprazole, rabeprazole, and sucralfate (medicines used to manage stomach ulcers)
Soya products and a high-fiber diet
Orlistat (a medicine used to reduce weight loss)
Propylthiouracil (used to manage hyperthyroidism)
Glucocorticoids (medicines used to manage inflammatory and autoimmune diseases) Ex. cortisone, prednisone
Propranolol (used to manage heart problems)
Lithium (used to manage mania)
Beta receptor blockers (medicines used to manage heart problems) Ex. propranolol, atenolol
Amiodarone (used to manage irregular heartbeats)
Iodinated contrast media (used in imaging techniques)
Salicylates (used to manage pain, fever, and inflammation) Ex. aspirin
Furosemide (used to manage heart problems)
Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin (used to manage fits)
Oestrogen based contraceptives (medicines used to manage fertilization) Ex. ethinylestradiol, norethindrone
Sertraline, amitriptyline, and imipramine (medicines used to manage depression)
Chloroquine or proguanil (used to manage malaria)
Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (Ex. imatinib and sunitinib)
Barbiturates
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum), an herbal medicine used to manage depression
Protease inhibitors, Ex. ritonavir (used to manage viral infections)
Methadone (used to manage pain)
5-flutouracil (used to manage cancer)
Coumarin derivatives (medicines used to manage blood clotting) Ex. warfarin
Digitalis (used to manage heart conditions)
Sympathomimetic agents (Ex. adrenaline), used to manage severe allergic reactions, cardiac arrest
Insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy Ex. metformin (used to manage diabetes mellitus)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more THYROACTIV 75MG TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Overdosage may cause hyperthyroidism, and symptoms include agitation, confusion, irritability, hyperactivity, headache, sweating, mydriasis, fast heartbeat, irregular heartbeat, fast breathing, fever, increased bowel movements, and fits. Psychiatric symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism may also occur, including affectability, fatigue, anxiety, and nervousness. In severe cases, it causes a thyrotoxic crisis and leads to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and coma.

Store THYROACTIV 75MG TABLET below 25°C

THYROUP 125MCG TABLET is not recommended for use if you have unmanageed hyperthyroidism, unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis, unmanageed adrenal insufficiency, or pituitary insufficiency. Consult your doctor before taking it.

THYROUP 125MCG TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking THYROUP 125MCG TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Cholestyramine, colestipol, clofibrate, simvastatin, and lovastatin (medicines used to manage high cholesterol levels in the blood)
Calcium, aluminium, magnesium, and iron supplements
Polystyrene sulfonates, kayexalate (used to manage high potassium levels in the blood)
Lanthanum, sevelamer (used to manage high phosphate levels in the blood)
Pantoprazole, rabeprazole, and sucralfate (medicines used to manage stomach ulcers)
Soya products and a high-fiber diet
Orlistat (a medicine used to reduce weight loss)
Propylthiouracil (used to manage hyperthyroidism)
Glucocorticoids (medicines used to manage inflammatory and autoimmune diseases) Ex. cortisone, prednisone
Propranolol (used to manage heart problems)
Lithium (used to manage mania)
Beta receptor blockers (medicines used to manage heart problems) Ex. propranolol, atenolol
Amiodarone (used to manage irregular heartbeats)
Iodinated contrast media (used in imaging techniques)
Salicylates (used to manage pain, fever, and inflammation) Ex. aspirin
Furosemide (used to manage heart problems)
Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin (used to manage fits)
Oestrogen based contraceptives (medicines used to manage fertilization) Ex. ethinylestradiol, norethindrone
Sertraline, amitriptyline, and imipramine (medicines used to manage depression)
Chloroquine or proguanil (used to manage malaria)
Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (Ex. imatinib and sunitinib)
Barbiturates
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum), an herbal medicine used to manage depression
Protease inhibitors, Ex. ritonavir (used to manage viral infections)
Methadone (used to manage pain)
5-flutouracil (used to manage cancer)
Coumarin derivatives (medicines used to manage blood clotting) Ex. warfarin
Digitalis (used to manage heart conditions)
Sympathomimetic agents (Ex. adrenaline), used to manage severe allergic reactions, cardiac arrest
Insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy Ex. metformin (used to manage diabetes mellitus)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more THYROUP 125MCG TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Overdosage may cause hyperthyroidism, and symptoms include agitation, confusion, irritability, hyperactivity, headache, sweating, mydriasis, fast heartbeat, irregular heartbeat, fast breathing, fever, increased bowel movements, and fits. Psychiatric symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism may also occur, including affectability, fatigue, anxiety, and nervousness. In severe cases, it causes a thyrotoxic crisis and leads to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and coma.

introduction:
Introduction About THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET

THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET contains Thyroxine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Synthetic thyroid hormones. It is used in the management of hypothyroidism. THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET is not recommended for use if you have unmanageed hyperthyroidism, unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis, unmanageed adrenal insufficiency, or pituitary insufficiency. Consult your doctor before taking it.

THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. Consult your doctor before taking it. THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET can be used safely in pregnant and breastfeeding women and requires dose adjustment. Consult your doctor before taking it.

The most common side effects of taking THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET are increased appetite, weight variations, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, changes in the menstrual cycle, fever, sensitivity to heat, cramps, and mood swings. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen.
usesDetails:

To manage hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:
How THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET Works

THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET contains thyroxine, which controls the entire metabolic activity of the body and is very important for the proper functioning of our body.
usageDetails:
How to use THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET

Take THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET in the morning on an empty stomach at least half an hour before breakfast or as directed by the physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending on your age, body weight, and disease condition.

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Cholestyramine, colestipol, clofibrate, simvastatin, and lovastatin (medicines used to manage high cholesterol levels in the blood)
Calcium, aluminium, magnesium, and iron supplements
Polystyrene sulfonates, kayexalate (used to manage high potassium levels in the blood)
Lanthanum, sevelamer (used to manage high phosphate levels in the blood)
Pantoprazole, rabeprazole, and sucralfate (medicines used to manage stomach ulcers)
Soya products and a high-fiber diet
Orlistat (a medicine used to reduce weight loss)
Propylthiouracil (used to manage hyperthyroidism)
Glucocorticoids (medicines used to manage inflammatory and autoimmune diseases) Ex. cortisone, prednisone
Propranolol (used to manage heart problems)
Lithium (used to manage mania)
Beta receptor blockers (medicines used to manage heart problems) Ex. propranolol, atenolol
Amiodarone (used to manage irregular heartbeats)
Iodinated contrast media (used in imaging techniques)
Salicylates (used to manage pain, fever, and inflammation) Ex. aspirin
Furosemide (used to manage heart problems)
Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin (used to manage fits)
Oestrogen based contraceptives (medicines used to manage fertilization) Ex. ethinylestradiol, norethindrone
Sertraline, amitriptyline, and imipramine (medicines used to manage depression)
Chloroquine or proguanil (used to manage malaria)
Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (Ex. imatinib and sunitinib)
Barbiturates
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum), an herbal medicine used to manage depression
Protease inhibitors, Ex. ritonavir (used to manage viral infections)
Methadone (used to manage pain)
5-flutouracil (used to manage cancer)
Coumarin derivatives (medicines used to manage blood clotting) Ex. warfarin
Digitalis (used to manage heart conditions)
Sympathomimetic agents (Ex. adrenaline), used to manage severe allergic reactions, cardiac arrest
Insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy Ex. metformin (used to manage diabetes mellitus)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Overdosage may cause hyperthyroidism, and symptoms include agitation, confusion, irritability, hyperactivity, headache, sweating, mydriasis, fast heartbeat, irregular heartbeat, fast breathing, fever, increased bowel movements, and fits. Psychiatric symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism may also occur, including affectability, fatigue, anxiety, and nervousness. In severe cases, it causes a thyrotoxic crisis and leads to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and coma.

Keep THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET out of the sight and reach of children
Store THYRONIL 12.5MCG TABLET below 25°C

introduction:
Introduction About THYROTAG 100MCG TABLET

THYROTAG 100MCG TABLET contains Levothyroxine which belong to the group of medicines known as Thyroid hormones. It is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is chemically identical to thyroxine produced by the thyroid gland. It helps in replacing missing thyroid hormone and in all forms of underactive thyroid function (hypothyroidism) or after the removal of the thyroid gland.  Thyroid hormone is vital for the normal growth and development. Lack of right number of thyroid hormones leads to slowing down in natural functions of our body.

Hypothyroidism is a condition where enough thyroid hormone required are not produced by the body. Some of the most common symptoms of hypothyroidism are tiredness, weight gain and feeling depressed. THYROTAG 100MCG TABLET helps in replacing the thyroxine that your thyroid gland cannot produce and manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism. Always take THYROTAG 100MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. 

Before taking this medicine tell your doctor if you have or ever had kidney disease, heart disease, or pancreas problems. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before taking this medicine. The most common side effects such as restlessness, insomnia, diarrhea, changes in menstrual cycle in women. Consult your doctor for advice if you experience any above side effects or it persists for a longer duration.
uses: In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce
To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism
usesDetails:
Uses Of THYROTAG 100MCG TABLET

It helps:

In replacing the thyroxine that the thyroid gland cannot produce
To manage the symptoms of hypothyroidism
mechanismOfAction:
How THYROTAG 100MCG TABLET Works

THYROTAG 100MCG TABLET is a synthetic thyroid hormone which is identical to natural occurring thyroid hormone thyroxine or T4, produced by the thyroid gland. Thyroxine regulates the production of another hormone called thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) which in turn controls how much thyroxine is produced. Levothyroxine regulates TSH production in the same way and therefore, substitutes for a lack of endogenous thyroxine (produced by the thyroid gland).

Take THYROTAG 100MCG TABLET exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush the medicine. Your doctor will prescribe the right dose depends on your age, body weight and disease condition.

Tell your doctor if you are taking or recently taken any other medicines, including medicines obtained without a prescription or the following:

Medicines used to manage diabetes
Anticoagulants such as warfarin, dicoumarol (used to thin the blood)
Amiodarone (used to manage some heart conditions)
Aspirin
Medicines containing oestrogen (e.g. used for hormone replacement therapy or oral contraceptives)
Antidepressants (e.g. sertraline and tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline, imipramine)
Chloroquine and proguanil (used in malaria and rheumatic diseases)
5-fluouracil, imatinib and sunitinib (used for abnormal outgrowth)
Medicines used to control the heart rate (such as digoxin)
Medicines that stimulate the sympathetic nervous system such as adrenaline
Carbamazepine, phenytoin or barbiturates (used to manage epilepsy or seizures)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally takes too much of THYROTAG 100MCG TABLET consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Signs of an overdose may include fever, chest pain (angina), racing or irregular heartbeat, muscle cramps, headache, restlessness, flushing, sweating, diarrhoea, shaking (tremor), difficulty sleeping (insomnia) and very high temperature (hyperpyrexia).

introduction:
Introduction About TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET

TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET contains Thyroxine, which belongs to the group of medicines called Synthetic thyroid hormones. It is used in the management of hypothyroidism. TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET is not recommended for use if you have unmanageed hyperthyroidism, unmanageed subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis, unmanageed adrenal insufficiency, or pituitary insufficiency. Consult your doctor before taking it.

TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET should be used with caution in patients with coronary heart disease such as acute myocardial infarction, acute myocarditis, acute pancarditis, angina pectoris, and hypertension. Consult your doctor before taking it. TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET can be used safely in pregnant and breastfeeding women and requires dose adjustment. Consult your doctor before taking it.

The most common side effects of taking TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET are increased appetite, weight variations, headache, vomiting, diarrhea, changes in the menstrual cycle, fever, sensitivity to heat, cramps, and mood swings. Consult your doctor if any of the side effects worsen.

How TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET Works

TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET contains thyroxine, which controls the entire metabolic activity of the body and is very important for the proper functioning of our body.
usageDetails:
How to use TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET

Take TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET in the morning on an empty stomach at least half an hour before breakfast or as directed by the physician. Swallow the medicine with a glass of water. Do not chew the medicine. Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending on your age, body weight, and disease condition.

Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before taking TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines:

Cholestyramine, colestipol, clofibrate, simvastatin, and lovastatin (medicines used to manage high cholesterol levels in the blood)
Calcium, aluminium, magnesium, and iron supplements
Polystyrene sulfonates, kayexalate (used to manage high potassium levels in the blood)
Lanthanum, sevelamer (used to manage high phosphate levels in the blood)
Pantoprazole, rabeprazole, and sucralfate (medicines used to manage stomach ulcers)
Soya products and a high-fiber diet
Orlistat (a medicine used to reduce weight loss)
Propylthiouracil (used to manage hyperthyroidism)
Glucocorticoids (medicines used to manage inflammatory and autoimmune diseases) Ex. cortisone, prednisone
Propranolol (used to manage heart problems)
Lithium (used to manage mania)
Beta receptor blockers (medicines used to manage heart problems) Ex. propranolol, atenolol
Amiodarone (used to manage irregular heartbeats)
Iodinated contrast media (used in imaging techniques)
Salicylates (used to manage pain, fever, and inflammation) Ex. aspirin
Furosemide (used to manage heart problems)
Anticonvulsants such as carbamazepine and phenytoin (used to manage fits)
Oestrogen based contraceptives (medicines used to manage fertilization) Ex. ethinylestradiol, norethindrone
Sertraline, amitriptyline, and imipramine (medicines used to manage depression)
Chloroquine or proguanil (used to manage malaria)
Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (Ex. imatinib and sunitinib)
Barbiturates
Rifampicin (used to manage tuberculosis)
St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum), an herbal medicine used to manage depression
Protease inhibitors, Ex. ritonavir (used to manage viral infections)
Methadone (used to manage pain)
5-flutouracil (used to manage cancer)
Coumarin derivatives (medicines used to manage blood clotting) Ex. warfarin
Digitalis (used to manage heart conditions)
Sympathomimetic agents (Ex. adrenaline), used to manage severe allergic reactions, cardiac arrest
Insulin or other anti-diabetic therapy Ex. metformin (used to manage diabetes mellitus)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally took more TOYOPHARMIN 100MCG TABLET, consult your doctor immediately or visit the nearby hospital. Overdosage may cause hyperthyroidism, and symptoms include agitation, confusion, irritability, hyperactivity, headache, sweating, mydriasis, fast heartbeat, irregular heartbeat, fast breathing, fever, increased bowel movements, and fits. Psychiatric symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism may also occur, including affectability, fatigue, anxiety, and nervousness. In severe cases, it causes a thyrotoxic crisis and leads to seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and coma.
